records.text: Removed tissue is mapped into selected blocks for examination. Its report describes the examined material, rather than every cell in the tumour or body.

Tumour-bed biopsy after neoadjuvant therapy (simple)
records.text: A biopsy after drug treatment samples parts of the former breast tumour bed. A negative sample can miss remaining cancer and does not by itself establish that surgery can be omitted.

effective.effectiveText: Core biopsy collects small cylinders of tissue; fine-needle aspiration collects cells or fluid. Both sample a site, and adequacy depends on the diagnostic question and intended tests.
A biopsy removes cells or tissue for examination. The sampled site, method and collection date set the limits of what its findings can show.
Removed tissue becomes interpretable through documented orientation and sampling that link microscopic and molecular findings to their locations.

A breast biopsy needle that uses suction to pull tissue into its side window and cut it, so several larger samples can be taken through one small cut in the skin, guided by mammogram, ultrasound or MRI.
Sampling the former tumour site after treatment can miss scattered residual cancer, so a negative biopsy needs its study population and sampling method.
Fixed, frozen and living tissue preserve different properties. A preparation that works for one test may not support another.
Sections, extractions and destructive tests consume stored tissue. Planning several tests requires knowing what material remains and which uses it must support.
RNA quality measurements describe the condition of extracted RNA. Their usefulness depends on the measurement workflow the material will enter.
A result needs to remain linked to the tissue or blood sample it came from. Dividing or extracting a specimen creates new material with its own history.
